title: HIV TDR and Subtype Testing Protocol
author: Jingrong Ye
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8ahhsb6

steps.title: Perform HIV Sequencing
steps.instruction: Conduct population-based sequencing of HIV protease and codons 1–300 of reverse transcriptase on all specimens using in-house methods.

substeps.instruction: Outsource sequencing to one of three commercial companies: Beijing Sino Geno Max Co., Ltd, Beijing Tsingke Biological technology Co., Ltd, or Beijing Tianyi Huiyuan Biological technology Co., Ltd.
Perform sequencing using an ABI 3500 Analyzer.

steps.title: Infer HIV Subtype
steps.instruction: Determine the HIV subtype of the sequences using automated tools and phylogenetic analysis.

substeps.instruction: Use Context-Based Modeling for Expeditious Typing (COMET)-HIV for automated subtyping.
For sequences classified as 'unassigned' by COMET, perform neighbor-joining phylogenetic analysis using Mega 6.0.
Estimate trees based on the Kimura 2-parameter Model with 1000 bootstrap replicates.

steps.title: Analyze Transmitted Drug Resistance (TDR)
steps.instruction: Estimate TDR prevalence and classify drug susceptibility levels in two steps.

substeps.instruction: Estimate TDR prevalence using the Stanford Calibrated Population Resistance (CPR) method, based on the WHO list of surveillance drug-resistant mutations 2009 (SDRM 2009) update.

For patients with at least one drug-resistant mutation, use the Stanford drug-susceptibility algorithm (version 8.5) to classify sequences as susceptible (Stanford level 1 or 2), low-level resistance (Stanford level 3), intermediate-level resistance (Stanford level 4), or high-level resistance (Stanford level 5) for specific drugs and drug classes (NRTIs, NNRTIs, and PIs).
